header.title: UTICalc (Pittsburgh)
header.subtitle: UTI probability in febrile children 2–23 months

why_this_matters: Close to 7% of children under 2 presenting to an emergency department with fever have a UTI, and urine collection in this age group usually means catheterization. UTICalc estimates each child's risk so testing and empiric treatment can be targeted. In its 2018 validation, the clinical model reduced testing by 8.1% compared with the AAP algorithm and missed no UTIs (vs 3 missed).

sections.heading: Who it's for
bullets: Febrile children 2 to 23 months old (derived in children with documented temperature ≥ 38 °C).
Not for infants under 2 months or children 24 months and older.

sections.heading: How it works
bullets: Step 1, clinical model: six yes/no questions (age < 12 months, Tmax ≥ 39 °C, prior UTI, female or uncircumcised male, other fever source, fever ≥ 48 h) give a pretest probability to decide whether to get urine.
Step 2, lab model: enter whatever is available (nitrite, leukocyte esterase, WBC/mm³, Gram stain bacteria) to update to a posttest probability that informs empiric treatment while awaiting culture.

sections.heading: Input pearls
bullets: WBC must be per mm³ (counting chamber); do not enter WBC/hpf.
Bacteria means Gram stain; do not substitute urinalysis bacteria.

link.label: Open UTICalc
link.offline_text: UTICalc runs on the University of Pittsburgh website and needs an internet connection.

clinical_takeaway: Calculate pretest probability before deciding on urine collection, then update it with urinalysis results before deciding on empiric antibiotics. The tool supports judgment; culture confirms the diagnosis.
